subject: DPA redline & role clarifications — telemetry / embeddings / transfer
messages:
From: Sanjeev Patel <sanjeev.patel@acme-health.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Katie Morris <katie.morris@acme-health.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redline + clarification on telemetry & embeddings roles

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this on. We've attached our DPA redline (v3) and a short questionnaire — two quick items we want to confirm before signing:

1) Role mapping: Acme needs clarity in the DPA that for the use-case we described (customer records + PII enrichment), Acme will remain the Controller and Redwood the Processor for API calls, but we need explicit language around embeddings generated from customer data — Acme expects those to be treated as "derived personal data" and covered by controller obligations.

2) Logs & telemetry: we need minimum visibility into request/response logs for debugging, but we also need guarantees that raw PII is not retained longer than necessary. Please confirm typical retention windows and whether debug logs contain any customer content.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: please attach your current subprocessor list and confirm whether Redwood will use SCCs for EU transfers or a different mechanism.

We want to move to DocuSign once we converge on these points. Can you get us a response by EOD Tuesday?

Best,
Sanjeev
---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:02:11 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline + clarification on telemetry & embeddings roles

Hannah / team —

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed Acme's redline and propose the following positions (high-level):

1) Roles / embeddings: Maintain our standard position: Redwood is a Processor for customer-provided content and a Processor for derived artifacts (including embeddings) where those artifacts are created solely from Customer Data. We *do not* concede Controller status for embeddings. Instead we will add explicit language that "Embeddings and other derived representations created by Redwood from Customer Data are processed on behalf of the Customer; Customer retains Controller responsibilities for the purposes of applicable data protection laws." This meets their ask about coverage while protecting our operational model.

Suggested clause (short):
"For clarity, any embeddings, vector representations, or other derived artifacts generated by Redwood from Customer Data shall be treated as Processed Data under this DPA and processed by Redwood on behalf of the Customer. The Customer remains the Controller of Customer Data for the purposes of determining lawful basis and notice obligations to data subjects."

2) Logs & telemetry: current defaults (as of platform policy): request/response logs containing full request/response bodies are retained for 30 calendar days and are automatically redacted for recognized PII patterns where possible. Aggregated telemetry and anonymized usage metrics are retained up to 24 months. Debug traces (full traces captured for troubleshooting) are retained up to 90 days and are only accessible to internal eng/support under strict access controls and logged access. We should add an explicit paragraph promising not to use Customer Content (including embeddings) for model training unless agreed (if Acme cares about that, we can sign).

3) Subprocessors & transfers: we will provide the CSV (Monica, please attach). Our standard approach is to list subprocessors and provide 30 days' notice of material changes. For EU transfers we use the European Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-processor SCCs) or equivalent transfer mechanism depending on jurisdiction; offer a clause committing to execute SCCs where required.

4) Execution: we can do DocuSign for the final DPA once redlines are agreed. I recommend we push the revised redline back with the slightly expanded "embeddings" clause above and the telemetry retention table. If they insist embeddings = Controller, escalate to product/legal for a tradeoff.

I'll prepare a redline with the small embedding clause and the telemetry table; Marcus/Monica please confirm retention numbers and CSV now so I can stitch into the doc.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:48:03 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline + clarification on telemetry & embeddings roles

Laura / Hannah — quick confirmation of numbers for the DPA table below (you can paste into the doc):

- Request / response logs (raw request metadata + bodies): retained 30 days; auto-redaction applied for common PII (SSNs, credit card numbers, obvious identifiers) but customers should not send sensitive unencrypted identifiers.
- Debug traces (technical traces captured when support captures full context): retained 90 days; access logged; retention extension only for active incident response with customer consent.
- Aggregated telemetry & anonymized metrics: retained 24 months (used for product analytics).
- Embeddings (persisted vectors): retained per customer config by default 365 days; can be set to 0 (ephemeral) on request for specific customers. Embeddings are stored encrypted at rest and not used for general model training unless contractually agreed.

Notes: debug traces can contain snippets of customer content when captured; we gate access and provide redaction tooling. I'll attach the current subprocessor CSV to Laura/Monica in a separate internal ticket.

-Marcus
Senior Product Manager, Platform
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Sanjeev / Katie — thanks for the redline and the detailed notes. We reviewed and propose the edits below as an interim redline:

- Roles: we propose the clause below clarifying embeddings are processed on behalf of the Customer; Customer remains Controller for Customer Data (see language in attached redline). This should address Acme's coverage question while preserving Redwood's operational model.
- Logs & telemetry: commit to 30-day retention for request/response logs (auto-redaction where practical), 90 days for debug traces (access logged), 24 months for aggregated telemetry, and default 365 days for persisted embeddings (customer-configurable, can be set to ephemeral).
- Subprocessors & transfers: attached current CSV of subprocessors; Redwood will provide 30 days' notice of material changes. For EU transfers, Redwood will execute SCCs where required (we can include the standard SCC exhibit).

If this looks acceptable we'll transmit the updated redline via DocuSign. Link to sign: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&acct=1234

Requested next steps: please review the redline we attached and, if acceptable, sign via the DocuSign link within 48 hours so we can finalize. We'll upload the executed DPA to the HubSpot deal record once completed.

Thanks and happy to hop on a 30-min call if you'd prefer to walk through the embedding wording.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
